story_facts_verified.action: Columbus City Council passed Ordinance 2569-2026 (agenda item CA-19) on Monday, Sept. 28, 2026 (Regular Meeting No. 41), listing 17 S. High St., the Huntington National Bank building, on the Columbus Register of Historic Properties as Listed Property CR #84, and declaring an emergency. Vote: 8 affirmative (Bankston, Barroso De Padilla, Day-Achauer, Dorans, Remy, Ross, Wyche, Hardin), 1 abstention (Melissa Green); motion by Emmanuel Remy, seconded by Christopher Wyche. Status 'Passed' per City Bulletin #40.
story_facts_verified.applicant_and_owner: Application by Melinda Shah / Schooley Caldwell (Applicant) in cooperation with Downtown Columbus, Inc. (Owner). Owner consent form received; HRC public hearing held Sept. 3, 2026; HRC voted unanimously to recommend listing under CC 3117.05 Criteria A and E.
story_facts_verified.emergency_justification: Verbatim from the ordinance: the listing 'will facilitate its eligibility for historic tax credits in conjunction with the planned rehabilitation and adaptive use of the building,' submitted as an emergency 'to allow its incorporation in a historic tax credit application,' and 'the deadline for 17 S. High St. to apply for the state historic tax credits is September 29th.' The ordinance notes a Certified Local Government (Columbus HRC) local-landmark ordinance, with its effective date, must accompany the state application.
story_facts_verified.building: 13-story structure built in 1926 on the converted and expanded 1903 Harrison Building; period of significance 1926-1965; described in the ordinance as a locally significant example of the Renaissance Revival style associated with the Huntington banking family. The Columbus Register boundary covers three Franklin County Auditor parcels (010-023445-00, 010-027309-00, 010-011453-00) and includes the 1984 retail spaces, single-story arcade, and glazed tower infill. (Secondary: Wikipedia lists architect Snyder & Babbitt and 168 ft; not asserted in the article.)
story_facts_verified.law_school_background: Per CREN's Sept. 14, 2026 reporting and independent origins (WOSU, The Lantern), Downtown Columbus, Inc. plans to lease the building to OSU's Moritz College of Law, opening fall 2029 (30-year lease with purchase option; trustees authorized at least a 20-year term in June 2026). Main floor becomes event/common space; upper floors become classrooms, law library and faculty offices; Huntington National Bank relocates its branch within the building by summer 2027.
story_facts_verified.state_program: The Ohio Historic Preservation Tax Credit (administered by the Ohio Department of Development with SHPO/Ohio History Connection) is, per the SHPO program page, 'a competitive program that receives applications bi-annually in March and September'; SHPO reviews the rehabilitation component (Parts 1 and 2) for 'historic building' status and compliance with the Secretary of the Interior's Standards. The Round 37 ODOD deadline fell in late September 2026 (application-guide PDF returned HTTP 404 this run; the specific credit percentage and per-project cap were not sourced and are not asserted in the article).
story_facts_verified.context_parallel: The same Sept. 28 session also listed 440 Taylor Ave., the Pilgrim School, on the register as CR #83 (Ordinance 2572-2026) under the same emergency tax-credit rationale -- evidence of a pattern of local historic listings used as prerequisites for the September state credit round.
story_facts_verified.original_contributions: Direct reading of the primary ordinance text (Bulletin #40, pulled and pdftotext-extracted this run), including the verbatim emergency justification and the recorded council vote; the framing of the designation as the first disclosed financing step for a renovation whose budget the Sept. 14 announcement left open; identification of the parallel Pilgrim School (CR #83) designation the same night; a plain-English explanation of the Certified Local Government prerequisite drawn from the ordinance's own words; and a CREN data card built from the verified facts.
story_facts_verified.limitations_stated: The listing enables eligibility but does not fund the work; neither the ordinance nor OSU's announcement discloses a renovation budget; tax-credit applications are not public while under review; an award is not guaranteed and would be decided later in the competitive round; building permits and the renovation budget have not been filed. The article makes no prediction and no transaction/investment advice.
